Pi extension: use private-ai (Privatemode) models as a provider

## Behavior

Registers `private-ai` as a Pi model provider backed by
[Privatemode](https://docs.privatemode.ai/) - an OpenAI-compatible chat
endpoint operated inside confidential computing environments by
[Edgeless Systems](https://www.privatemode.ai/). No Pi service is involved.

### Connection modes

The connection is configured via the `privateAi` settings key (user settings
`~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or project settings `.pi/settings.json`):

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `privateAi.mode` | `"proxyless"` | `"proxyless"` uses the hosted [proxyless API](https://docs.privatemode.ai/api/proxyless-api/) (memory encryption, no client-side attestation). `"proxy"` calls a locally running [Privatemode proxy](https://docs.privatemode.ai/api/proxy-configuration/), which verifies the backend attestation and encrypts prompts client-side. |
| `privateAi.proxyBaseUrl` | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | Base URL of the proxy in `"proxy"` mode (e.g. a remote proxy at `http://raspberrypi:3003/v1`). |
| `privateAi.proxyApiKey` | `$PRIVATEMODE_API_KEY` | API key sent to the proxy in `"proxy"` mode. Supports `$ENV` interpolation, a literal value, or `!command` (like models.json). |

Example:

```json
{
  "privateAi": {
    "mode": "proxy",
    "proxyBaseUrl": "http://raspberrypi:3003/v1"
  }
}
```

Settings changes require a pi restart or `/reload`.

### Models

The following chat models appear under the `private-ai` provider
(see the [Privatemode model overview](https://docs.privatemode.ai/models/overview/)):

| Model ID | Alias | Context | Input | Reasoning effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `glm-5.3` | `glm-latest` | 1M | text | low / high / max |
| `glm-5.3-flash` | `glm-flash-latest` | 1M | text, image | low / high / max |
| `gpt-oss-120b` | - | 128k | text | low / medium / high |

- All models stream, support tool calling and always perform reasoning; the pi
  thinking level is forwarded as `reasoning_effort` and the `reasoning` field
  of the response is shown as thinking.
- Embedding, speech-to-text and the DeepSeek-OCR-2 models are not exposed
  (they are not chat models / need a special prompt format).
- Privatemode prices are EUR per million tokens
  ([pricing](https://docs.privatemode.ai/pricing/)); the EUR values are used
  as-is for the cost display.

### Authentication

Create an API key in the [Privatemode portal](https://docs.privatemode.ai/portal/api-keys/)
and store it exactly like any other provider credential:

```
/login private-ai
```

Pi prompts `Enter API key` and saves the credential in `auth.json`; the models
then appear in `/models` (and `/logout private-ai` removes it again).

Alternatives, in precedence order:

1. `auth.json` via `/login private-ai` (stored credential wins over everything below)
2. `PRIVATEMODE_API_KEY` environment variable: `export PRIVATEMODE_API_KEY="<your-api-key>"`
3. `privateAi.proxyApiKey` from settings (proxy mode only; supports `$ENV`
   interpolation, literals, or `!command`)

Without any credential the models are registered but hidden from the picker,
like every other provider - Pi suggests `/login` in that case.

Project-level `.pi/settings.json` values apply at session start (after
project trust); the extension reads `privateAi` from the user-level
`settings.json` directly at load so the models are known without a session
(`pi --list-models`, startup model selection).

## Installation

Local (development):

```bash
pi -e ./extensions/piagent-private-ai.ts
```

As a pi package (GitHub):

```bash
pi install git:https://github.com/FloezWerk/piagent-private-ai.git
```

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/private-ai` | Show provider status: connection mode, base URL, the resolved auth source, the current model (if it is a private-ai model) and the available models. |
| `/private-ai <model-id>` | Switch the current session to a `private-ai` model, e.g. `/private-ai glm-latest`. |

After changes in a running session: `/reload`.

## Dependencies

`@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and
`@earendil-works/pi-tui` are bundled by pi and are therefore only declared as
`peerDependencies`.
